_comment: SPIKE A fixtures — the reference text for each supported language.
WHY THESE SENTENCES. Each fixture is chosen to exercise the failure mode the
match step exists to catch, not to be easy. Every one contains at least one
token whose SPOKEN form differs from its DISPLAY form — a numeral, an
abbreviation, a symbol, or a year. Those are exactly the places where the
predicted-alignment design broke (spec 6.2) and where the observed->display
match must now prove itself. A fixture of plain prose would pass trivially
`expect_hard` names the display substrings we KNOW will not appear verbatim
in a transcript. If a run reports 100% matched and these were not resolved by
the normalizer path, the harness is measuring the wrong thing.

ROUTING CORRECTED 2026-08-09 (owner): es and fr are FISH AUDIO s2-pro, not Gemini. Gemini entered the routing table only as the Haitian Creole path; ht was removed from scope on 2026-08-08, so Gemini left with it. The first SPIKE A run measured es/fr against Gemini audio -- a provider the product will not ship -- which makes that half of the result an artifact of the wrong input, not a measurement of the design.

VOICE CORRECTED 2026-08-09 (owner): the es fixture was using Jacynthe, an ENGLISH Fish voice, to read Spanish. Fish s2-pro is multilingual so it produced audio, but an English-accented voice reading Spanish is not what ships and is not what should be measured -- it degrades recognition for a reason that has nothing to do with the design. motionmax's Fish roster has no Spanish voice, so this ID comes from Fish's own catalogue, filtered to languages=['es']. fr was already correct (Miriam, French Female).
fr voice set to Mario (French Male, d12dae2d...) 2026-08-09 per owner. Robert (a5d7dcbb...) is the alternate; both are French Male s2-pro from the reference stack's roster.

fr voice is Robert (a5d7dcbb..., French Male). THE LOCK RATIONALE IS WITHDRAWN 2026-08-09 (J29-M5). This line read: 'LOCKED to Robert ... Miriam 88.2%, Mario 94.4%, Robert 100% agreement within 250 ms. VOICE CHOICE IS A WORD-SYNC VARIABLE -- a 12-point swing with nothing else changed.' Every part of that is now known to be wrong. (1) Those figures are agree_within_250ms_pct on a word-vs-SEGMENT comparison (out/spike-a-crossengine.json:54), not this bar and not comparable to it. (2) n was 17-18 tokens on one 8-second clip; resolving a 12 pp effect at the observed discordance needs at least 35. (3) Re-measured at chapter length -- 1186 display words per clip, replicate pairs per voice, out/spike-a-voices.json -- the WITHIN-voice noise floor is 0.1 pp and the largest BETWEEN-voice difference is 1.9 pp at p=0.056, with 0 of 2 pairs significant. The 12-point swing does not reproduce; it was one token. Robert stays as the fr voice because it is the reference stack roster choice, NOT because it aligns better. (4) Separately and more importantly: the best long clip of any voice scores 71.4% against the bar of 95, and any_clip_passes_bar is false.

HOLDOUT added 2026-08-09: different text, same voices. The per-language calibration offset is FIT on `languages` and SCORED on `holdout`. Fitting and scoring on one clip would choose a parameter that makes the bar pass, which is what the pre-fixed drift bound and language scope exist to prevent -- the discipline has to apply to calibration too or it is theatre.

PARAGRAPH added 2026-08-09 (Probe) for H26-M7. The entire corpus above is 62.5 seconds, 8-12 s per clip, so the failure the bar exists to catch -- drift ACCUMULATING across a chapter -- cannot appear by construction. `paragraph` is >=60 s of speech per language, same providers and voices, one TTS call each. The WORD COUNTS differ by language on purpose -- 224 en, 222 es, 293 fr -- because the three voices do not speak at the same rate. Robert (fr) runs at 4.2 words/s against Adam's 3.1, so an equal-word-count fixture would have given fr 38 s of audio and en 49 s, and the constraint that matters for accumulation is SECONDS, not words. Equalising the wrong axis is how a corpus comes to test three different things. It carries the same hard-token doctrine as `languages`: numerals, an abbreviation, a year, a thousands separator in each locale's own convention (1,800 / 1.800 / 1 800). It has NO ground truth -- it is one natural utterance -- so it is used to ask whether timestamp error grows with POSITION, not to measure absolute error. Read groundtruth.py for what that probe can and cannot see.

en.text: The committee met on March 14th to review 8 proposals. Prof. Adams noted that costs rose by 12 percent since 2019, reaching 3,400 euros per unit.

en.text: The reading group met on the first Tuesday of every month, and by the end of the year it had worked through 14 books. Dr. Alvarez, who founded the group in 2011, kept a ledger of every title, the number of pages, and the number of members who finished it. In March the average was 62 percent; by November it had risen to 88 percent. The longest book ran to 940 pages and took three sessions to discuss. The shortest, at 112 pages, took a single evening. Members paid 5 euros a month toward coffee, which came to 1,800 euros over the life of the group. When the library closed for renovation in 2023, the group moved to a room above the bakery on Mill Street, where it still meets on the first Tuesday, and where the ledger is still kept by hand, in ink, rather than on a screen of any kind. Attendance peaked at 31 people in the spring of 2016 and settled near 18 after that. The founder stepped down in 2021, citing 2 knee operations and a move to the coast, but she still sends a list of 6 recommendations every January. The group has never once cancelled a meeting, not even in the week the roof leaked and 400 volumes had to be carried upstairs in a single evening.

es.text: El grupo de lectura se reunía el primer martes de cada mes, y al terminar el año había leído 14 libros. La Dra. Álvarez, que fundó el grupo en 2011, llevaba un registro de cada título, del número de páginas y del número de socios que lo terminaban. En marzo el promedio era del 62 por ciento; en noviembre había subido al 88 por ciento. El libro más largo tenía 940 páginas y ocupó tres sesiones enteras. El más corto, de 112 páginas, ocupó una sola tarde. Los socios pagaban 5 euros al mes para el café, lo que sumó 1.800 euros durante la vida del grupo. Cuando la biblioteca cerró por obras en 2023, el grupo se mudó a una sala encima de la panadería de la calle Molino, donde sigue reuniéndose el primer martes, y donde el registro se sigue llevando a mano y no en una pantalla. La asistencia llegó a 31 personas en la primavera de 2016 y se estabilizó cerca de 18 después. La fundadora dejó el cargo en 2021, tras 2 operaciones de rodilla y una mudanza a la costa, pero sigue enviando una lista de 6 recomendaciones cada enero. El grupo nunca ha cancelado una reunión, ni siquiera la semana en que el techo goteó y hubo que subir 400 volúmenes en una sola tarde.

fr.text: Le groupe de lecture se réunissait le premier mardi de chaque mois, et à la fin de l'année il avait lu 14 livres. Le Dr Alvarez, qui a fondé le groupe en 2011, tenait un registre de chaque titre, du nombre de pages et du nombre de membres qui l'avaient terminé. En mars la moyenne était de 62 pour cent ; en novembre elle était montée à 88 pour cent. Le livre le plus long comptait 940 pages et a occupé trois séances entières. Le plus court, de 112 pages, n'a occupé qu'une seule soirée. Les membres payaient 5 euros par mois pour le café, ce qui a fait 1 800 euros sur la durée du groupe. Quand la bibliothèque a fermé pour travaux en 2023, le groupe a déménagé dans une salle au-dessus de la boulangerie de la rue du Moulin, où il se réunit toujours le premier mardi, et où le registre est toujours tenu à la main. La fréquentation a atteint 31 personnes au printemps 2016 et s'est stabilisée autour de 18 par la suite. La fondatrice a quitté ses fonctions en 2021, après 2 opérations du genou et un déménagement sur la côte, mais elle envoie toujours une liste de 6 recommandations chaque mois de janvier. Le groupe n'a jamais annulé une seule séance, pas même la semaine où le toit a fui et où il a fallu déplacer 400 volumes en une soirée. Le registre compte aujourd'hui 1 240 pages, reliées en 4 volumes, et le bibliothécaire en a fait une copie numérique en 2024 sans jamais accepter de se séparer de l'original, qui reste dans une armoire fermée à clé derrière le comptoir, avec les 3 stylos qui ont servi à le tenir depuis le premier jour.
